airplane: visible aircraft body with wings and tail, compact object-level structure, and clear airplane contours, distinguishing airplane from airport by lacking broad aviation-area context, from parking_lot by lacking open vehicle-row pavement, and from runway by being a discrete aircraft object rather than a long paved strip.
airport: large aviation area with broad paved runways and airport-related infrastructure, distinguishing airport from runway by broader aviation context, from airplane by lacking a single compact fuselage object, and from rectangular_farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel boundaries.
baseball_diamond: compact sports field with a clear diamond-shaped infield and surrounding outfield, distinguishing baseball_diamond from golf_course by lacking expansive landscaped fairways, from ground_track_field by lacking an oval running track, and from stadium by weaker enclosure and spectator-related structure.
basketball_court: small rectangular hard-court surface with clear sports markings, distinguishing basketball_court from tennis_court by court layout and line pattern, from baseball_diamond by lacking a diamond-shaped infield, and from parking_lot by lacking vehicle-row organization.
beach: bright shoreline region with clear sand-water boundary and open coastal texture, distinguishing beach from desert by direct water contact, from island by lacking a fully isolated landmass, and from sea_ice by sandy coastal texture rather than frozen surface.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land, distinguishing bridge from river by being a crossing rather than a watercourse, from harbor by lacking strong dock-side port context, and from freeway by lacking a long continuous multi-lane road corridor.
chaparral: dry shrub-covered terrain with coarse natural texture and sparse woody vegetation, distinguishing chaparral from desert by slightly richer vegetation texture, from forest by lacking dense continuous canopy, and from wetland by lacking mixed shallow-water vegetation patches.
church: prominent religious building or complex with distinctive landmark-like architecture, distinguishing church from palace by less expansive ceremonial layout, from commercial_area by weaker dense business-block texture, and from medium_residential by lacking repeated neighborhood housing patterns.
circular_farmland: cultivated land with large regular circular irrigation patterns, distinguishing circular_farmland from rectangular_farmland by round parcel geometry, from storage_tank by broader agricultural texture around the circles, and from river by lacking a continuous winding water channel.
cloud: bright amorphous atmospheric mass with soft edges and no stable ground texture, distinguishing cloud from sea_ice by lacking a flat frozen-surface appearance, from river by lacking a continuous channel boundary, and from mountain by lacking stable terrain relief.
commercial_area: dense urban business district with organized building blocks, roads, and large man-made structures, distinguishing commercial_area from church by lacking landmark-like religious structure, from industrial_area by weaker factory-yard organization, and from intersection by stronger building dominance rather than road-junction geometry.
dense_residential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing, distinguishing dense_residential from medium_residential by much closer building intervals, from mobile_home_park by less uniform trailer-row organization, and from commercial_area by smaller repeated residential roofs rather than larger business blocks.
desert: broad barren region with dry homogeneous texture and very little vegetation, distinguishing desert from chaparral by weaker shrub texture, from mountain by less terrain relief, and from beach by lacking a clear shoreline water boundary.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with dark green natural texture, distinguishing forest from meadow by stronger canopy continuity, from freeway by lacking a paved linear transport corridor, and from chaparral by denser vegetation cover.
freeway: wide multi-lane transportation corridor with continuous linear flow and road-network structure, distinguishing freeway from overpass by emphasizing extended roadway rather than a local elevated crossing, from intersection by lacking a compact junction node, and from runway by lacking aviation-strip context.
golf_course: large landscaped green field with fairways, lawns, and designed open-course layout, distinguishing golf_course from baseball_diamond by lacking a compact diamond infield, from meadow by stronger man-made landscaping, and from beach by lacking shoreline water context.
ground_track_field: sports venue with an oval running track and central field, distinguishing ground_track_field from stadium by weaker enclosure and spectator structure, from baseball_diamond by lacking a diamond-shaped infield, and from tennis_court by lacking small repeated rectangular court geometry.
harbor: waterfront maritime area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent port infrastructure, distinguishing harbor from ship by broader dock-and-shore context, from mobile_home_park by lacking repeated residential rows, and from bridge by lacking a simple narrow crossing structure.
industrial_area: large factory-like compounds with heavy infrastructure, storage yards, and production-oriented layouts, distinguishing industrial_area from thermal_power_station by weaker plant-specific heavy layout, from storage_tank by not being dominated only by circular tanks, and from parking_lot by stronger factory-compound structure.
intersection: road junction where multiple transportation lines meet, distinguishing intersection from freeway by emphasizing a compact node rather than a long corridor, from roundabout by lacking a central circular traffic island, and from overpass by weaker elevated overlap structure.
island: landmass completely surrounded by water with clear shoreline boundary, distinguishing island from beach by being an enclosed landform rather than a shoreline strip, from river by lacking a narrow continuous channel shape, and from sea_ice by stable land texture rather than frozen surface.
lake: large enclosed inland water body with smooth water surface and clear boundary, distinguishing lake from wetland by more uniform open water, from sea_ice by liquid-water appearance rather than frozen texture, and from desert by clear water dominance.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture and weak structural boundaries, distinguishing meadow from rectangular_farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel boundaries, from forest by lacking dense continuous canopy, and from wetland by weaker water-vegetation fragmentation.
medium_residential: moderately spaced residential houses with visible yards and neighborhood streets, distinguishing medium_residential from mobile_home_park by less uniform trailer-row structure, from dense_residential by larger spacing, and from sparse_residential by denser neighborhood grouping.
mobile_home_park: repetitive small elongated housing units arranged in orderly rows, distinguishing mobile_home_park from medium_residential by stronger trailer-like regularity, from dense_residential by more uniform layout, and from harbor by lacking dock-water organization.
mountain: rugged elevated terrain with strong relief, slope shadows, and irregular topographic texture, distinguishing mountain from desert by stronger terrain variation, from snowberg by less snow-dominant brightness, and from cloud by more stable terrain-like structure.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation, distinguishing overpass from freeway by its bridge-like crossing form, from intersection by stronger elevated overlap pattern, and from bridge by emphasizing road-over-road transport structure.
palace: large landmark complex with symmetrical layout, open courtyards, and prominent architecture, distinguishing palace from church by more expansive ceremonial organization, from commercial_area by weaker dense urban block texture, and from tennis_court by lacking small repeated sports-court markings.
parking_lot: large open paved area with organized parking rows and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parking_lot from industrial_area by lacking dense factory compounds, from mobile_home_park by lacking repeated trailer-like housing rows, and from harbor by lacking strong dock-water context.
railway: elongated rail corridor with parallel tracks and linear transport structure, distinguishing railway from railway_station by lacking a concentrated station hub, from freeway by rail-line texture rather than paved multi-lane roadway, and from industrial_area by clearer linear track organization rather than factory compounds.
railway_station: transport hub with concentrated rail lines and station-related structures, distinguishing railway_station from railway by stronger station-node organization, from industrial_area by clearer rail concentration, and from airport by lacking aviation-runway context.
rectangular_farmland: cultivated land divided into regular rectangular parcels, distinguishing rectangular_farmland from circular_farmland by angular field boundaries, from terrace by lacking stepped contour bands, and from meadow by stronger man-made agricultural organization.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks, distinguishing river from desert by clear water dominance, from island by lacking a fully enclosed landmass, and from rectangular_farmland by lacking regular cultivated parcel boundaries.
roundabout: circular traffic junction with a central island and radiating roads, distinguishing roundabout from intersection by the visible circular center, from industrial_area by lacking factory-compound texture, and from medium_residential by lacking repeated residential roofs.
runway: long straight paved strip with elongated linear geometry and open airport-like surroundings, distinguishing runway from airport by weaker terminal-scale context, from freeway by lacking complex road branching, and from parking_lot by lacking compact vehicle-row organization.
sea_ice: bright frozen surface with irregular cracked or slab-like texture over water, distinguishing sea_ice from snowberg by flatter ice-field appearance, from lake by frozen-surface texture rather than open water, and from island by lacking stable land texture.
ship: discrete vessel object on water with elongated hull-like structure, distinguishing ship from harbor by lacking broad dock-side context, from sea_ice by clear object boundaries and vessel shape, and from island by lacking stable landform texture.
snowberg: bright snow- or ice-covered elevated landform with strong cold-tone texture, distinguishing snowberg from mountain by stronger snow coverage, from sea_ice by stronger landform-like relief, and from cloud by more stable terrain-like structure.
sparse_residential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density, distinguishing sparse_residential from medium_residential by much larger spacing, from mobile_home_park by lacking uniform trailer-row organization, and from rectangular_farmland by repeated roof structures rather than crop parcels.
stadium: large sports complex with prominent field and stronger enclosure or spectator-related structure, distinguishing stadium from ground_track_field by more venue-like framing, from baseball_diamond by larger scale, and from thermal_power_station by lacking heavy industrial plant structure.
storage_tank: clusters of large circular industrial tanks with highly regular round geometry, distinguishing storage_tank from thermal_power_station by emphasizing tank clusters, from industrial_area by stronger circular-container dominance, and from circular_farmland by lacking surrounding agricultural field texture.
tennis_court: small rectangular court surfaces with clear line markings and repeated court geometry, distinguishing tennis_court from medium_residential by lacking roof clusters, from basketball_court by different court layout and line pattern, and from mobile_home_park by lacking trailer-row housing structure.
terrace: stepped agricultural or hillside bands following slope contours, distinguishing terrace from rectangular_farmland by contour-aligned layered structure, from mountain by clearer repeated stepped agricultural bands, and from desert by more organized slope-based land use.
thermal_power_station: large power-generation complex with heavy industrial structures, chimneys, or cooling-related facilities, distinguishing thermal_power_station from storage_tank by broader power-plant infrastructure, from industrial_area by more plant-specific heavy layout, and from commercial_area by lacking dense urban business-block structure.
wetland: water-rich natural area with mixed shallow water and vegetation patches, distinguishing wetland from lake by more fragmented water-vegetation texture, from river by weaker continuous channel structure, and from island by lacking a solid enclosed landmass.
